newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares jump on Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares jump on Beirut bourse.

text.p: Bank shares jumped ahead on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Thursday with Banque Audi and Bank of Beirut hitting new highs.
BOB announced a higher than expected 72.5 percent rise in mid-year net profits to $4.09 million and brokers said they expected to share to rise further as a result.
The other two listed banks, Audi and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce have not yet issued their mid-year results. Brokers say they expect them to be strong.
The LIBX bank index rose 3.09 percent to 172.31. The LISPI general index climbed 0.95 percent to 90.49 and the BLOM general index rose 0.96 percent to 957.80.
Turnover took a steep fall to 153,177 from 264,641 for a value of $1,768,979 against $2,704,760.
Banque Audi hit a record high for the second day running, jumping to $27 from $26.250. Bank of Beirut rose to $4.375 from $4.1875 and BLC climbed to $19.625 from $19.250.
"There was heavy demand for Audi and Bank of Beirut. Our customers are still interested in these banks," said a broker who requested anonymity.
Commenting on BOB's mid-year results, another broker said: "These results are higher than expectations. There is still room for the share to rise."
Solidere A increased to $10.75 from $10.5 with demand outstripping supply. Solidere B fell to $11 from $11.125 in strong demand.
There was no trade in the four industrial firms, Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
